plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.2.10
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the tetrahedron bounded by the coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y using a double integral. The figure contains two linked diagrams. Left: a 3D perspective showing the tetrahedron in xyz-space with vertices at (0, 0, 4), (1, 0, 0), and (0, 2, 0), bounded above by the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (labeled on the slanted face) with the base region R labeled. Right (inset): the 2D base region R in the xy-plane, a right triangle with vertices at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 2), bounded by the x-axis, y-axis, and the line y = 2 - 2x; a red vertical strip illustrates the inner integration limits from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x. An arrow connects the two diagrams. The figure establishes the correspondence between the 3D tetrahedron and the triangular base R over which the iterated double integral is set up.

elements: 3D coordinate axes with arrowheads: z-axis vertical up, y-axis to the screen-right, x-axis toward lower-left (toward viewer)
axis labels 'x', 'y', 'z' at the arrow tips
tetrahedron bounded by the three coordinate planes and the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y
slanted front face of the tetrahedron (the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y) drawn as a pale teal filled triangle with vertices (0,0,4), (1,0,0), (0,2,0)
triangular base region R in the xy-plane with vertices (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,2,0), shaded pale teal and labeled 'R'
vertical triangular face in the yz-plane (x=0): vertices (0,0,0), (0,2,0), (0,0,4)
vertical triangular face in the xz-plane (y=0): vertices (0,0,0), (1,0,0), (0,0,4)
teal vertex dots at (0,0,4), (1,0,0), (0,2,0)
axis tick labels '4' on z, '2' on y, '1' on x

2D inset panel: xy-plane axes with horizontal x-axis (arrow right, label 'x') and vertical y-axis (arrow up, label 'y'), origin labeled '0'
2D triangular region R with vertices (0,0), (1,0), (0,2), shaded pale teal, labeled 'R'
teal hypotenuse segment from (0,2) to (1,0) labeled 'y = 2 - 2x'
tick labels '2' on the y-axis and '1' on the x-axis of the 2D panel, with teal dots at (0,2) and (1,0)
red vertical integration strip in the 2D panel from y = 0 up to y = 2 - 2x at a chosen x

interactions.teaches: The inner integral sweeps y from 0 up to the boundary y = 2 - 2x for a fixed x; the height of the red strip shrinks linearly as x moves from 0 to 1, and the corresponding vertical slice of the solid rises to the slanted plane.

interactions.label: Slicing plane z = c
interactions.teaches: Horizontal cross-sections of the tetrahedron are similar triangles whose legs shrink from 1 and 2 at z = 0 to 0 at z = 4, so the integration bounds 0 ≤ y ≤ 2 - 2x are just the z = 0 slice.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The triangular region R in the xy-plane is exactly the shadow (projection) of the tetrahedron, so the double integral over R with integrand 4 - 4x - 2y gives the volume.
Seeing the tetrahedron from other angles confirms that the slanted face meets the axes at 4, 2 and 1 and that R lies flat in the xy-plane.

demo_steps.title: The base region R
demo_steps.narration: Start in the xy-plane: R is the right triangle with legs along the axes, capped by the line y = 2 - 2x (set z = 0 in the plane equation).

demo_steps.title: Inner integral: sweep in y
demo_steps.narration: Drag the red strip. At each fixed x the strip runs from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x, which are the inner limits of integration.

demo_steps.title: Lift into 3D
demo_steps.narration: The same triangle is the base of the tetrahedron; above each point of R the solid extends up to the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y, the integrand.

demo_steps.title: Horizontal slices
demo_steps.narration: Raise the slicing plane: the cross-section stays a similar triangle with vertices sliding along the edges, vanishing at the apex (0, 0, 4).

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World units equal graph units. 3D panel occupies screen-left, centered near world origin: x-axis from 0 to about 1.6 pointing toward lower-left (toward the viewer), y-axis from 0 to about 2.8 pointing screen-right, z-axis from 0 to about 4.8 pointing straight up; arrowheads on all three. Tetrahedron vertices: origin (0,0,0), (1,0,0) on x, (0,2,0) on y, (0,0,4) on z. Slanted face = plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y (equivalently 4x + 2y + z = 4). Base region R = {0 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ 2 - 2x}. Volume = ∫₀¹∫₀^{2-2x}(4-4x-2y) dy dx = 4/3. Horizontal slice at height c: triangle with legs x ≤ (4-c)/4 and y ≤ (4-c)/2. The 2D inset sits to the RIGHT of and slightly BELOW the top of the 3D panel, roughly two-thirds up the frame, drawn front-on as a flat plot with its OWN axis convention: horizontal axis = x (0 to 1.4, label 'x' at right arrow), vertical axis = y (0 to 2.4, label 'y' at top arrow) — note this is a rotated/flipped view of the 3D xy-plane, which the linking arrow conveys. Red integration strip is a vertical segment at x ≈ 0.55 from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x, ~2px wide. Large cream block arrow (#FBE3B8 fill, #999999 outline, ~1.5 units tall) curves from beneath the 2D panel leftward and up into the base region R. Palette: filled triangles pale teal #C4E6E0 at ~0.55 opacity, boundary/hypotenuse strong teal #00A6A0 (2-3px), vertex dots #00A6A0 radius ~0.06, axes and tick text black, red strip #F4525A, slicing plane a translucent gray-teal #8FCFC8 at 0.3 opacity with a teal outlined cross-section triangle.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the tetrahedron's four faces as separate THREE.Mesh triangles with DoubleSide MeshBasicMaterial (flat, unlit, matching the print look) plus LineSegments edges in teal; keep the interior faces visible by using low opacity and depthWrite false. Axes as Line + ConeGeometry arrowheads. Labels ('x','y','z','4','2','1','R','z = 4 - 4x - 2y') as CSS2DObject/sprite HTML so they stay upright while orbiting. The 2D inset is best drawn either as an orthographic second scene rendered to a viewport on the right half of the canvas, or as an SVG/HTML overlay — either way its drag handle maps pointer x to the parameter x ∈ [0,1], and that same x drives a highlighted vertical quad in the 3D scene spanning y ∈ [0, 2-2x], z ∈ [0, 4-4x-2y] so the two panels stay in sync. The slicing plane is a clipped triangle recomputed each slider frame, not a big plane with clipping planes, so its vertices visibly ride the tetrahedron edges. Default camera: standard isometric-style pose matching the source (z up, y to the right, x toward lower-left); heightFraction 0.6.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the red vertical integration strip in the 2D base panel and watch the corresponding cross-section highlight on the 3D plane z=4-4x-2y update in real time
- Slider for the slicing-plane height: the triangular cross-section expands or contracts inside the tetrahedron while its vertices stay on the edges, showing how bounds of integration change with the plane.

discrepancies: The generated 3D panel draws the full closed tetrahedron (faint yz and xz faces plus a gray O–z edge), whereas the source shades only the slant plane and the base region R — the solid reads as a filled body rather than the source's two shaded triangles.
A red vertical slice triangle is drawn inside the 3D solid; the source has a red strip only in the 2D panel.

Axis orientation differs slightly: in the source the y axis runs horizontally to the right and x points to the lower-left with z strictly vertical; here y is tilted down-right, making the base region R more foreshortened than the source's clearly readable base triangle.

Relative panel scale/placement differs: the 2D inset is markedly smaller than the 3D panel and sits close to the y-axis arrow and the '2' label, producing a more crowded composition than the well-separated side-by-side panels of the source.
The inset's region R fill and hypotenuse are correct, but the red strip in the 2D panel is drawn with a circular drag handle dot not present in the source.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-labelled reconstruction of both panels plus the linking block arrow with excellent, mathematically correct interactions (strip slider/drag, z=c slicing plane, view toggles, guided steps); main weaknesses are added geometry (closed tetrahedron faces, in-solid red slice) and a crowded, smaller 2D inset with a slightly rotated axis convention versus the source.
action_items: Remove or further fade the extra yz/xz faces and the gray O–z edge so only the slant plane and base R are shaded, matching the source's two-triangle look.
Reposition/enlarge the 2D inset so it is comparable in height to the 3D panel and clear of the y-axis arrow and '2' label, restoring the source's clean side-by-side composition.
Rotate the 3D view so the y axis reads nearly horizontal to the right and x drops to the lower-left, as in the source, keeping z strictly vertical.
Make the in-3D red strip appear only when the strip/inner-integral demo step is active, so the default view matches the source figure.

The 2D inset sits to the RIGHT of and slightly BELOW the top of the 3D panel, roughly two-thirds up the frame, drawn front-on as a flat plot with its OWN axis convention: horizontal axis = x (0 to 1.4, label 'x' at right arrow), vertical axis = y (0 to 2.4, label 'y' at top arrow) — note this is a rotated/flipped view of the 3D xy-plane, which the linking arrow conveys. Red integration strip is a vertical segment at x ≈ 0.55 from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x, ~2px wide. Large cream block arrow (#FBE3B8 fill, #999999 outline, ~1.5 units tall) curves from beneath the 2D panel leftward and up into the base region R. Palette: filled triangles pale teal #C4E6E0 at ~0.55 opacity, boundary/hypotenuse strong teal #00A6A0 (2-3px), vertex dots #00A6A0 radius ~0.06, axes and tick text black, red strip #F4525A, slicing plane a translucent gray-teal #8FCFC8 at 0.3 opacity with a teal outlined cross-section triangle.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the tetrahedron's four faces as separate THREE.Mesh triangles with DoubleSide MeshBasicMaterial (flat, unlit, matching the print look) plus LineSegments edges in teal; keep the interior faces visible by using low opacity and depthWrite false. Axes as Line + ConeGeometry arrowheads. Labels ('x','y','z','4','2','1','R','z = 4 - 4x - 2y') as CSS2DObject/sprite HTML so they stay upright while orbiting. The 2D inset is best drawn either as an orthographic second scene rendered to a viewport on the right half of the canvas, or as an SVG/HTML overlay — either way its drag handle maps pointer x to the parameter x ∈ [0,1], and that same x drives a highlighted vertical quad in the 3D scene spanning y ∈ [0, 2-2x], z ∈ [0, 4-4x-2y] so the two panels stay in sync. The slicing plane is a clipped triangle recomputed each slider frame, not a big plane with clipping planes, so its vertices visibly ride the tetrahedron edges. Default camera: standard isometric-style pose matching the source (z up, y to the right, x toward lower-left); heightFraction 0.6.

interactions.teaches: The inner integral sweeps y from 0 up to the boundary y = 2 - 2x for a fixed x; the height of the red strip shrinks linearly as x moves from 0 to 1, and the corresponding vertical slice of the solid rises to the slanted plane.

interactions.label: Slicing plane z = c
interactions.teaches: Horizontal cross-sections of the tetrahedron are similar triangles whose legs shrink from 1 and 2 at z = 0 to 0 at z = 4, so the integration bounds 0 ≤ y ≤ 2 - 2x are just the z = 0 slice.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The triangular region R in the xy-plane is exactly the shadow (projection) of the tetrahedron, so the double integral over R with integrand 4 - 4x - 2y gives the volume.
Seeing the tetrahedron from other angles confirms that the slanted face meets the axes at 4, 2 and 1 and that R lies flat in the xy-plane.

demo_steps.title: The base region R
demo_steps.narration: Start in the xy-plane: R is the right triangle with legs along the axes, capped by the line y = 2 - 2x (set z = 0 in the plane equation).

demo_steps.title: Inner integral: sweep in y
demo_steps.narration: Drag the red strip. At each fixed x the strip runs from y = 0 to y = 2 - 2x, which are the inner limits of integration.

demo_steps.title: Lift into 3D
demo_steps.narration: The same triangle is the base of the tetrahedron; above each point of R the solid extends up to the plane z = 4 - 4x - 2y, the integrand.

demo_steps.title: Horizontal slices
demo_steps.narration: Raise the slicing plane: the cross-section stays a similar triangle with vertices sliding along the edges, vanishing at the apex (0, 0, 4).
